reading.body:
The Model Context Protocol's server reference repository alone has accumulated nearly 90,000 stars, more than the six language SDKs and the registry combined, which signals that practitioners are building and sharing MCP servers faster than they are reaching for the formal client libraries.

Across eight repositories the total star count reaches roughly 159,000, all of them actively pushed to within the week before this data was generated. No repository is archived. That combination, high attention and recent activity across every entry, suggests the tooling layer around MCP is still in a phase of rapid accumulation rather than consolidation. Python leads the SDK tier with around 24,000 stars, TypeScript follows at roughly 13,000, and Go, C#, Java, and a visual inspector tool for testing servers account for the remainder. The Go SDK is maintained in collaboration with Google, the C# SDK with Microsoft, and the Java SDK with Spring AI, meaning three of the six language implementations carry named corporate co-maintainers.

Five of the eight repositories carry custom licences rather than standard open-source terms, with only the Python and Java SDKs under MIT. That licensing split matters for anyone building commercial tooling on top of these libraries, but the data does not describe what the custom licences permit or restrict. The data also covers only the official modelcontextprotocol organisation on GitHub and says nothing about third-party registries, community forks, or actual deployment volumes, so star counts here are an indicator of developer interest, not of compute consumed or inference workloads served.
